speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with the timeline: when did these symptoms first begin, and have they been getting worse gradually or suddenly? Also, could you describe exactly where you feel the weakness in your right leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: That rapid progression over just one week is concerning; have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or blurred fields, and do you experience any numbness or tingling in your legs? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of nonenhancing white matter lesions are suggestive of demyelination or vascular changes; have you experienced any urinary incontinence, sexual dysfunction, or balance issues that appeared before the leg weakness? REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System.

The combination of acute multifocal neurological deficits (leg weakness, gait instability), subacute cognitive decline (forgetfulness, executive dysfunction), and behavioral changes (paranoia, agitation) alongside non-enhancing white matter lesions on MRI is highly suggestive of an inflammatory vasculopathy affecting the CNS. The rapid progression over one week distinguishes this from typical multiple sclerosis. We should proceed with a lumbar puncture to analyze cerebrospinal fluid for inflammatory markers and to rule out infectious or neoplastic etiologies immediately.
